title: Android 17 has some new tricks to keep your web traffic private
summary: Here's how Android 17 is locking down your network traffic from prying eyes.
body: TL;DR Google’s implementing a number of new network security upgrades for Android 17. Encrypted Client Hello attempts to solve DNS privacy problems by encrypting server lookups. SMS Blaster protection empowers carriers to block low-security 2G connections by default. Keeping mobile devices secure is one of those jobs that never end, and when it comes to security in Android, Google finds itself constantly working to lock our phones down against external threats. With Android 17 , the company’s already highlighted some of the big ways it’s been improving security , and today Google has a few more updates to share on how your phone is becoming more secure and private that ever. Android 17 makes a number of changes to how devices work with network traffic. One big privacy-protecting one there impacts how apps are able to see your home’s local network, preventing them from probing it for fingerprinting or even spotting vulnerable network hardware. Another we knew about implements Certificate Transparency by default, helping ensure that your phone uses the proper SSL certificates for the server it’s trying to communicate with.

title: How Los Dos de Tamaulipas Turn Relatable Stories Into Norteño Hits: ‘We Want to Leave a Legacy Here’
summary: Meet Billboard's Latin Up-And-Comer Artist of the Month for August.
body: Before they became Los Dos de Tamaulipas, 25-year-old twins Orlando and Rolando Zapata performed as Los Cuates de Tamaulipas. The name changed, but the family connection — and the pride they feel for their parents’ home state — remains at the center of the Houston-based group’s identity. The duo began playing music in 2014, when Rolando picked up the accordion and Orlando followed a month later on the bajo quinto. They were around 13 years old, learning old-school norteño songs and performing at local restaurants, quinceañeras and birthday parties. “We’re the first in our family to be musicians,” Orlando tells Billboard over Zoom. What began as a way to earn tips gradually became a career. Orlando and Rolando later expanded the group with drummer Julián Pérez and their cousin Christian García, who have been part of the band for about seven years. Today, Orlando serves as the group’s lead vocalist and bajo quinto player, while Rolando plays accordion and sings harmony. Together, they have developed a norteño sound anchored by lively accordion riffs, bajo quinto chords and passionate harmonies. As storytellers, they draw from heartbreak, ambition, faith, gratitude, regional pride an…

title: YouTube just brought back the videos users thought they had lost
summary: Your saved videos in Watch Later and other playlists should now be showing up where they belong.
body: TL;DR YouTube has confirmed it fixed the bug that was hiding videos from Watch Later and other playlists. Affected users reported missing videos, ‘playlist does not exist’ errors, and broken playlists across mobile and desktop. YouTube hasn’t said what caused the issue or whether an app update is needed, but affected users should now see their full playlists again. Watch Later is one of those YouTube features you don’t appreciate until it stops working. It is the easiest way to stash a video you don’t have time for, build a queue for later, or simply keep track of something you don’t want to lose. So, having videos mysteriously disappear from the playlist over the past few weeks has understandably been frustrating for some users. The good news is that YouTube says the problem is now fixed. YouTube confirmed the fix in a forum post earlier today, telling affected users that all their videos should now display correctly in their playlists, including Watch Later on the YouTube app.

The restart is triggered as part of a harmless time zone update, but the watch seemingly refuses to turn on after that. Thankfully, the smartwatch can reportedly be brought back to life by placing it on the charging puck. Samsung’s Galaxy Watch variants consistently rank among the best smartwatches in the business. However, like with any hardware, bugs and glitches can pop up from time to time, and we can now report on one such case involving Samsung’s premium smartwatch model. According to SamMobile , a Galaxy Watch Ultra at their disposal was prompted to restart after a time zone update. It’s not uncommon for this message to appear, particularly if you’ve switched time zones recently. However, the site found that the smartwatch refused to boot after pressing restart.

body: If there’s one thing we all want from our next smartphone , it’s more battery life. Thankfully, battery cells are bigger than ever, while processors are increasingly frugal. However, some phones are definitely better than others at lasting through more demanding work/life balances or taking lighter users through a second day. The upcoming release is expected to be the final beta before the stable One UI 9 rollout for the Galaxy S26. Stable One UI 9 arrived last month with the launch of Samsung’s latest foldables: the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8, and the Z Flip 8. Despite the stable release, older phones still lack the update. Samsung continues to run a beta and recently released the sixth One UI 9 beta for the Galaxy S26 series only this week. The fact that the latest One UI beta release consisted mostly of bug fixes and usability-related enhancements — and that a stable version is already available for certain devices — led to hopes that a stable release would come soon. title: The budget Android phone is quietly on its way to extinction
summary: Cheap phones are disappearing as premium models take the spotlight.
body: TL;DR IDC projects a record 16.7% drop in global smartphone shipments for 2026 due to severe memory shortages. Sub-$100 Android devices are disappearing as average selling prices jump 27.6% to $581. Buyers are shifting toward premium devices and foldables, with Apple’s September 9 event expected to accelerate growth in the category. Walking into a retail shop with $250 used to mean leaving with a stellar budget handset that punched well above its weight class. That reality started slipping away earlier this year when Android sales tanked 14% in the US , giving us an early hint of broader supply troubles ahead. Fast forward to today, and store displays look completely different. Cheap options are quietly vanishing, mid-range price tags are creeping upward, and IDC’s latest quarterly forecast confirms what we have all been sensing: the era of the budget smartphone is officially over. According to IDC’s August 2026 report , worldwide smartphone shipments are expected to plummet by a record 16.7% this year. That marks a sharp downward revision from the 13.9% decline projected back in May.

title: Google says it fixed the playlist bug driving Home users crazy
summary: Your smart speaker should stop mangling your playlist requests.
body: Credit: Brady Snyder / Android Authority TL;DR Google says it has fixed an issue that caused Google Home devices to play the wrong playlists. Users had reported getting unrelated songs, albums, or playlists instead of what they asked for. Google hasn’t explained what caused the problem, and we’re awaiting user confirmation that the fix has worked. However well you’re getting along with your Google smart speaker, the least you’d expect it to do right is play the correct music when you ask for it. Apparently, that hasn’t always been the case lately. After a YouTube Music playback bug affecting Nest Hubs a couple of months ago, Google now says it has fixed another issue that frustrated Home users requesting playlists. The company responded today to at least two recent threads on the r/googlehome subreddit , where users had complained that Google Home devices were playing the wrong music when asked for a specific playlist. Google’s official Nest Community account said, “We fixed the issue that was causing the wrong playlists to play,” and asked users to report back if they’re still experiencing it.

title: Google sounds like it’s got a fix for Keep list glitches… maybe?
summary: Finally, you can finish your shopping list additions!
body: TL;DR Google Home users recently began reporting issues adding items to their Keep lists. Google has now responded to those reports, although confusingly references “UI issues.” The company’s fix is expected to hit devices within the next few days. You try so hard to be an organized adult: planning ahead, making lists, and keeping track that you get done what you need to. While we have plenty of great tools at our disposal for helping out with that kind of thing, they don’t always work how they’re meant to, and earlier this week we shared with you that Google Home devices were seemingly losing the ability to add new items to Google Keep lists. While that was quite frustrating, it sounds like Google is nearly ready to deploy a fix… kind of? Let’s back up a second, first. Historically, Google Assistant was happy to let you modify lists to your heart’s content, but back in 2023 Google locked that down to restrict third-party apps . Critically, though, lists in Keep were supposed to stay right on working. And while that’s been the case for a while now, users recently started complaining that Gemini on Google Home devices seems completely unable to meaningfully add to their Keep lists.

title: Meta will pay $18 billion for teen safety, asks TikTok and YouTube to follow suit
summary: The settlement also adds mandatory time limits and other default safeguards across Instagram and Facebook.
body: TL;DR Meta has agreed to pay $18 billion as part of a settlement with 52 attorneys general over claims that Facebook and Instagram negatively impact teen mental health. The company has also implemented new default safeguards for teens that restrict access to core functions like Reels and Stories during certain times of the day. Around $5.3 billion of the overall $18 billion payout is conditioned on industry rivals TikTok and YouTube adopting similar measures. For a while now, multiple studies have attempted to demonstrate how social media apps can have a detrimental impact on teen mental health. Meta-owned platforms like Instagram and Facebook have been at the center of discussions about the negative impact on children, and that’s led to some high-profile lawsuits. Today, Meta is ending one long legal battle by announcing a settlement with 52 attorneys general. In a statement on its blog, Meta said it will pay around $18 billion as part of the settlement to fund youth online safety initiatives, along with other state activities. It further announced a long list of teen-safety features it will bundle into Facebook and Instagram, while also making some options the default for all te…

title: The Galaxy S27 Ultra battery upgrade could have been much wilder
summary: A 7,000mAh battery may have been on the table for the S27 Ultra.
body: TL;DR Samsung reportedly tested a 7,000mAh Galaxy S27 Ultra battery, but ultimately backed away from the idea. The current target is said to be 5,700mAh to 6,000mAh, potentially enabled by silicon-carbon battery tech. The unconfirmed leak also hints at S27 Ultra prototypes without the S Pen and a new Samsung over-ear headset. For years, Samsung has watched rivals turn battery capacity into a numbers game while the Galaxy S Ultra line remained stuck at 5,000mAh. That figure hasn’t changed since 2020, even as 6,000mAh and 7,000mAh batteries become increasingly common on competing Android flagship phones . Now, a new leak suggests Samsung may have secretly tested its own 7,000mAh option for the Galaxy S27 Ultra, only to back away from it this time. The 7,000mAh version was reportedly one of several prototypes. But Samsung is now rumored to be targeting a 5,700mAh to 6,000mAh battery instead, which is still a sizeable jump that could finally give the Galaxy S Ultra line the capacity boost it’s needed for years.

title: The Galaxy S26 Ultra just achieved a first for Android phone sales
summary: Samsung is the sole Android brand in the top 10, but the S26 Ultra also made a notable achievement.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra was the most popular Android phone globally in Q2 2026, according to a new report. This is apparently the first time that an “ultra-premium” phone led Android sales in Q2. The base Galaxy S26 also made the list, along with three Galaxy A phones. The most popular Android phones in a quarter tend to be cheap models. That’s not a surprise, as the lower prices make these phones more accessible than high-end models. However, the latest global market share report reveals a surprising top-seller for Android. Counterpoint Research has posted its Q2 2026 global market share report , and it turns out that the $1,300 Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra was the most popular Android phone in the quarter. Samsung’s Ultra phone was ranked fourth. What’s also interesting is that the base Galaxy S26 landed in ninth place. By contrast, the Galaxy S25 Ultra was in ninth place back in Q2 2025 while the base S25 didn’t feature at all.

title: Google Photos may soon give you less time to restore deleted media

body: Credit: Taylor Kerns / Android Authority TL;DR Google Photos currently keeps backed-up media in the Trash for 60 days and regular, non-backed-up media for 30 days. Code found in Google Photos v7.90 indicates Google plans to unify this rule, reducing trash retention for all media to 30 days. Google appears to be preparing a notable shift in Google Photos, shortening the time deleted photos and videos sit in your trash folder before they vanish forever. While Google has been spotted working on smarter backup solutions, such as overnight backup options , this upcoming change could rationalize how long your discarded media hangs around. If you’re looking to configure a really impressive smart home, Google Home automations are your best friend. While routines are great for pulling off complicated multi-device workflows, automations take that to the next level by, well, automating them — instead of manually activating a routine, automations begin all by themselves when their starter event occurs. At least, that’s the way things are supposed to work, but right now there’s a frustrating glitch impacting automations tied to TVs. Over on Reddit’s Google Home sub, users have been complaining about automations involving their TVs that fail to work . The 1999 platform fighter hasn’t been available through official means for several years and isn’t currently playable on Nintendo Switch consoles. We aren’t aware of any ports made from the newly decompiled code yet, but we expect they’ll start appearing soon. Aside from some high-profile rereleases, present-day Nintendo is notoriously stingy when it comes to providing easy, legitimate access to its immense back catalog of classic games. This, in part, has inspired fans to take matters into their own hands by decompiling old favorites, recreating their source code so the games can be easily (if unofficially) ported to modern platforms like Windows or Android. Now, another classic that’s been inaccessible on modern hardware is ripe for porting: 1999’s Super Smash Bros. has been fully decompiled. As shared on Decomp.dev , Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 is now “100.00% decompiled,” meaning the game’s source code has been completely recreated and it’s ready to be ported.
